label: Help me respond
description: A useful response to the latest meeting question
prompt: Use the live meeting transcript to identify the latest question or request directed to the user. State that question briefly, then give a concise, natural response they can say aloud. Use the user's real supplied experience and facts; never invent personal experience. If it is unclear which question needs answering, say so and ask one focused clarification. Do not invent an unanswered question.

label: What did I miss?
description: Catch up on the latest discussion and questions
prompt: Help the user rejoin the live meeting using only the captured transcript. Briefly explain the current topic, the most recent important points, and the latest question or decision that may need their attention. Distinguish an explicit question to the user from a general question. Suggest one useful way to rejoin. Do not claim to know speech that was not captured. Keep it concise.

label: Revisit a topic
description: Jump back to something important in the meeting
prompt: Find the user-specified topic in the captured meeting transcript. Summarize what was actually said, any decisions or unresolved questions, and a useful way to bring it back into the conversation. Keep the original discussion separate from new suggestions. If the topic is not in the captured transcript, say that clearly and ask for the missing context.

label: Action items
description: Pull out decisions, owners, and next steps
prompt: Extract actionable points from the captured meeting transcript. Separate explicitly agreed commitments from proposed next steps. For each confirmed action give the task, owner only if stated, and deadline only if stated. Mark missing owners or deadlines as unspecified. Briefly list important unresolved decisions if relevant. Do not turn suggestions into commitments or invent action items. If none were captured, say so.

label: Follow-up questions
description: Ask something relevant to the discussion
prompt: Suggest up to three specific, high-value questions the user could ask in the current live meeting. Ground them in the captured transcript, avoid questions already answered, and rank by usefulness. If the captured context does not support a useful question, explain what is missing instead of inventing a discussion.

label: Meeting recap
description: Review the key points captured in this meeting
prompt: Give a concise recap of the captured meeting transcript: key points, confirmed decisions, and open questions. Distinguish agreed facts from proposals. Use only captured content and keep it under 150 words unless a specific user request needs more detail.

label: Draft a follow-up
description: Turn the meeting into a clear follow-up message
prompt: Draft a short follow-up message based on the captured meeting transcript. Include confirmed decisions, agreed actions with stated owners and deadlines, and genuine unresolved questions. Do not invent attendees, names, decisions, or commitments. Use neutral wording when a recipient is unknown. Provide a draft only; do not claim it was sent.

label: Summarize this chat
description: Bring the current conversation into focus
prompt: Summarize the previous turns in this assistant chat only. Cover the user's goal, useful conclusions, and outstanding questions. Do not imply this was a recorded meeting or draw on an unrelated meeting transcript. Keep the summary concise.

label: Next steps
description: Turn this chat into a practical plan
prompt: Use the previous turns of this assistant chat to propose up to five concrete next steps toward the user's goal. Distinguish your recommendations from actions the user already committed to. Do not invent completion, owners, or deadlines, and do not use an unrelated meeting transcript.

label: Explain more simply
description: Make the last answer easier to understand
prompt: Explain the most recent assistant answer in this chat more simply, focusing on what the user was trying to understand. Preserve its factual meaning and correct any evident error. Use one concrete example if helpful. Do not refer to an unrelated meeting.

label: Analyze screen
description: Make sense of what is in front of you
prompt: Focus on the current screen. Identify the main task, question, or error and give the most useful answer or next action first. Use only legible details; never guess unreadable text or an unseen cause. Separate observations from inferences. Use conversation context only if directly relevant. If no screenshot is available, say so. Do not provide a generic inventory or repeat unrelated conversation history.
